reactions.notes: Forms pinacols; a reductive C-C bond forming reaction.

reactions.name: McMurry reaction
reactions.conditions: Low-valent titanium reagent from TiCl3 or TiCl4 with zinc.
reactions.observation: Two ketones couple to give an alkene.
reactions.notes: Forms alkenes from carbonyls, often with stereoselectivity.

reactions.name: Wittig reaction
reactions.conditions: A phosphorus ylide reacts with an aldehyde or ketone.
reactions.observation: A C=C bond forms; triphenylphosphine oxide is the by-product.
reactions.notes: The stereochemistry is controlled by the ylide type.

reactions.name: Horner-Wadsworth-Emmons reaction
reactions.conditions: A phosphonate carbanion with an aldehyde or ketone.
reactions.notes: A modified Wittig reaction using a phosphonate.

reactions.name: Peterson olefination
reactions.conditions: An alpha-silyl carbanion adds to a carbonyl, then acid or base eliminates.
reactions.notes: A silicon-based alternative to the Wittig reaction.

reactions.name: Julia olefination
reactions.conditions: A phenyl sulfone carbanion reacts with an aldehyde, then reduction eliminates.
reactions.notes: Efficient for making dienes in complex syntheses.

reactions.name: Clemmensen reduction
reactions.conditions: Zinc amalgam and hot concentrated hydrochloric acid.
reactions.observation: A carbonyl is reduced to a methylene group.
reactions.notes: Works under acidic conditions; complements Wolff-Kishner.

reactions.name: Wolff-Kishner reduction
reactions.conditions: Hydrazine and strong base at high temperature.
reactions.observation: A carbonyl is reduced to a methylene group with nitrogen released.
reactions.notes: Performed under basic conditions; complements Clemmensen.

reactions.name: Baeyer-Villiger oxidation
reactions.conditions: A peroxyacid (mCPBA) or peroxide with a ketone.
reactions.observation: A ketone is converted into an ester or lactone.
reactions.notes: The migration order follows the group's migratory aptitude.

reactions.name: Ozonolysis
reactions.conditions: Ozone at low temperature, followed by a reducing workup.
reactions.observation: The alkene double bond is cleaved to carbonyls.
reactions.notes: Used to locate double bonds in unknown alkenes.

reactions.name: Prilezhaev epoxidation
reactions.conditions: A peroxyacid such as mCPBA or peracetic acid.
reactions.observation: An epoxide forms across the double bond.
reactions.notes: A stereospecific syn addition.

reactions.name: Sharpless asymmetric epoxidation
reactions.equation: allylic alcohol + Ti(OiPr)4, (+)-DET, TBHP --> chiral epoxide
reactions.conditions: Titanium tetraisopropoxide, a chiral tartrate, and tert-butyl hydroperoxide.
reactions.observation: One enantiomer of the epoxide forms in high excess.
reactions.notes: A landmark in asymmetric catalysis.

reactions.name: Syn dihydroxylation
reactions.conditions: Catalytic osmium tetroxide with a co-oxidant such as NMO.
reactions.notes: Upjohn and Sharpless variants are used in synthesis.

reactions.name: Hydroboration-oxidation
reactions.equation: alkene + BH3.THF, then H2O2/OH- --> anti-Markovnikov alcohol
reactions.conditions: Borane followed by alkaline hydrogen peroxide.
reactions.observation: An alcohol forms with anti-Markovnikov regiochemistry and syn addition.
reactions.notes: A key route to primary alcohols from terminal alkenes.

reactions.name: Oxymercuration-demercuration
reactions.equation: alkene + Hg(OAc)2/H2O, then NaBH4 --> Markovnikov alcohol
reactions.conditions: Mercury(II) acetate in water, then sodium borohydride.
reactions.observation: A Markovnikov alcohol forms with no rearrangement.
reactions.notes: Avoids the carbocation rearrangements of acid-catalyzed hydration.

reactions.name: Markovnikov addition of HBr
reactions.conditions: Hydrogen halide added to an unsymmetrical alkene.
reactions.observation: The hydrogen adds to the carbon with more hydrogens.
reactions.notes: Proceeds through the more stable carbocation.

reactions.name: Anti-Markovnikov addition (peroxide effect)
reactions.conditions: HBr with peroxides or light present.
reactions.observation: The bromine adds to the less substituted carbon.
reactions.notes: A free-radical chain mechanism; only HBr shows it.

reactions.name: Wacker process
reactions.conditions: Palladium(II) chloride with copper(II) chloride co-catalyst.
reactions.notes: An industrial route to acetaldehyde from ethylene.

reactions.name: Hydroformylation (oxo process)
reactions.equation: RCH=CH2 + CO + H2 --Co or Rh--> RCH2CH2CHO + RCH(CH3)CHO
reactions.conditions: Syngas with a cobalt or rhodium catalyst.
reactions.observation: An aldehyde with one extra carbon forms.
reactions.notes: A major industrial route to aldehydes and alcohols.

reactions.name: Fischer esterification
reactions.conditions: A carboxylic acid and an alcohol with an acid catalyst.
reactions.observation: An ester with a pleasant smell forms; the reaction is reversible.
reactions.notes: Water must be removed to drive the equilibrium.

reactions.name: Transesterification
reactions.conditions: An ester and an alcohol with an acid or base catalyst.
reactions.observation: The alkoxy group of the ester is exchanged.
reactions.notes: Used to make biodiesel from triglycerides.

reactions.name: Acid-catalyzed ester hydrolysis
reactions.conditions: Dilute acid and heat.
reactions.observation: The ester is cleaved back into acid and alcohol.
reactions.notes: The reverse of Fischer esterification.

reactions.name: Amide coupling with DCC
reactions.conditions: A carbodiimide such as DCC activates the acid.
reactions.notes: The basis of solid-phase peptide synthesis with HOBt.

reactions.name: Gabriel synthesis
reactions.equation: phthalimide + KOH + R-X, then H2NNH2 --> RNH2
reactions.conditions: Potassium phthalimide with an alkyl halide, then hydrazinolysis.
reactions.observation: A primary amine forms without over-alkylation.
reactions.notes: Uses the phthalimide anion as a protected nitrogen nucleophile.

reactions.name: Strecker amino acid synthesis
reactions.equation: RCHO + NH3 + HCN, then hydrolysis --> RCH(NH2)COOH
reactions.conditions: An aldehyde, ammonia, and hydrogen cyanide, then acid hydrolysis.
reactions.notes: A classical route to amino acids.

reactions.name: Acetoacetic ester synthesis
reactions.equation: CH3COCH2COOC2H5 --base, R-X, then H3O+, heat--> CH3COCH2R
reactions.conditions: Alkylation of ethyl acetoacetate then acidic decarboxylation.
reactions.notes: Builds ketones by adding alkyl groups to an active methylene.

reactions.name: Malonic ester synthesis
reactions.equation: CH2(COOC2H5)2 --base, R-X, then H3O+, heat--> RCH2COOH
reactions.conditions: Alkylation of diethyl malonate then hydrolysis and decarboxylation.
reactions.notes: Builds carboxylic acids via an active methylene.

reactions.name: Stork enamine alkylation
reactions.equation: ketone + R2NH --H+--> enamine --R'-X, H3O+--> alpha-alkyl ketone
reactions.conditions: A secondary amine forms an enamine, which is then alkylated.
reactions.notes: Regioselective alpha-alkylation of ketones.

reactions.name: Friedel-Crafts alkylation
reactions.conditions: An alkyl halide with anhydrous aluminium chloride.
reactions.observation: An alkyl group replaces an aromatic hydrogen.
reactions.notes: Carbocation rearrangements and polyalkylation are common.

reactions.name: Friedel-Crafts acylation
reactions.conditions: An acyl chloride with anhydrous aluminium chloride.
reactions.notes: No rearrangement and little polyacylation, unlike alkylation.

reactions.name: Nitration of benzene
reactions.conditions: Concentrated nitric and sulfuric acids.
reactions.observation: Nitrobenzene forms; the mixture is a pale yellow liquid.
reactions.notes: The nitronium ion NO2+ is the electrophile.

reactions.name: Sulfonation of benzene
reactions.conditions: Fuming sulfuric acid (oleum).
reactions.notes: The sulfonic acid group is a useful water-solubilizing group.

reactions.name: Halogenation of benzene
reactions.conditions: Bromine or chlorine with an iron or aluminium halide catalyst.
reactions.notes: A Lewis acid polarizes the halogen into an electrophile.

reactions.name: Reimer-Tiemann reaction
reactions.conditions: Chloroform and strong base with phenol.
reactions.observation: A formyl (aldehyde) group enters the ring next to the hydroxyl.
reactions.notes: Proceeds through dichlorocarbene.

reactions.name: Kolbe-Schmitt reaction
reactions.conditions: Sodium phenoxide heated under carbon dioxide pressure.
reactions.observation: A carboxyl group enters next to the hydroxyl.
reactions.notes: The industrial route to salicylic acid and aspirin.

reactions.name: Vilsmeier-Haack reaction
reactions.conditions: Dimethylformamide and phosphorus oxychloride.
reactions.notes: Uses an iminium electrophile for formylation.

reactions.name: Williamson ether synthesis
reactions.conditions: A sodium alkoxide with a primary alkyl halide.
reactions.observation: An ether forms via SN2 substitution.
reactions.notes: Primary halides avoid the competing elimination.

reactions.name: Finkelstein reaction
reactions.conditions: An alkyl halide with sodium iodide in acetone.
reactions.notes: Driven by precipitation of the insoluble sodium chloride.

reactions.name: Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction
reactions.conditions: Bromine with a phosphorus catalyst at the alpha-carbon.
reactions.notes: The route to alpha-amino and alpha-hydroxy acids.

reactions.name: Wohl-Ziegler bromination
reactions.conditions: N-bromosuccinimide with light or a radical initiator.
reactions.observation: Bromination occurs at the allylic position.
reactions.notes: A selective radical benzylic or allylic halogenation.

reactions.name: Diels-Alder reaction
reactions.conditions: A conjugated diene and a dienophile, often with heat.
reactions.observation: A six-membered ring forms in a single step.
reactions.notes: A suprafacial [4+2] cycloaddition with high stereospecificity.

reactions.name: Retro-Diels-Alder reaction
reactions.conditions: Heat reverses the [4+2] cycloaddition.
reactions.observation: The ring fragments into a diene and a dienophile.
reactions.notes: Used in mass spectrometry and protecting-group strategies.

reactions.name: Huisgen cycloaddition (click chemistry)
reactions.conditions: A copper(I) catalyst joins an azide and a terminal alkyne.
reactions.observation: A 1,4-disubstituted triazole forms quickly and cleanly.
reactions.notes: The archetypal click reaction, used in bioconjugation.

reactions.name: SN1 substitution
reactions.conditions: A tertiary alkyl halide in a polar protic solvent.
reactions.notes: Proceeds through a carbocation; first-order in the substrate.

reactions.name: SN2 substitution
reactions.conditions: A primary alkyl halide with a strong nucleophile.
reactions.notes: A one-step, concerted backside attack; second-order.

reactions.name: E1 elimination
reactions.conditions: A tertiary substrate in a polar protic solvent with heat.
reactions.observation: The more substituted alkene usually forms.
reactions.notes: Shares a carbocation intermediate with SN1.

reactions.name: E2 elimination
reactions.conditions: A strong bulky base such as potassium tert-butoxide.
reactions.observation: Concerted anti-periplanar loss of H and X.
reactions.notes: Follows Zaitsev's rule unless the base is bulky.

reactions.name: E1cb elimination
reactions.conditions: A substrate with an acidic beta-hydrogen, under base.
reactions.observation: A carbanion (enolate) forms before the leaving group departs.
reactions.notes: Common with beta-hydroxy carbonyls and beta-halo acids.

reactions.name: Hofmann elimination
reactions.conditions: Exhaustive methylation then heating of the quaternary hydroxide.
reactions.notes: A bulky trimethylammonium leaving group controls regiochemistry.

reactions.name: Cope elimination
reactions.conditions: A tertiary amine oxide heated, often without solvent.
reactions.observation: A syn elimination gives the alkene.
reactions.notes: A mild, cis-selective elimination.

reactions.name: Chugaev elimination
reactions.conditions: A xanthate ester pyrolysed at about 200 degrees.
reactions.observation: An alkene forms by syn elimination.
reactions.notes: A thermal, base-free dehydration of alcohols.

reactions.name: Wurtz reaction
reactions.conditions: Two alkyl halides with sodium metal in dry ether.
reactions.notes: Works best for symmetrical products; side reactions occur.

reactions.name: Wurtz-Fittig reaction
reactions.conditions: An aryl halide and an alkyl halide with sodium.
reactions.notes: A way to attach alkyl chains to aromatic rings.

reactions.name: Grignard with formaldehyde
reactions.conditions: A Grignard reagent with formaldehyde.
reactions.observation: A primary alcohol with one extra carbon forms.
reactions.notes: A standard way to lengthen a carbon chain by one.

reactions.name: Grignard with an aldehyde
reactions.equation: RMgX + R'CHO, then H3O+ --> secondary alcohol
reactions.conditions: A Grignard reagent with an aldehyde other than formaldehyde.
reactions.notes: The nucleophile adds to the carbonyl carbon.

reactions.name: Grignard with a ketone
reactions.equation: RMgX + R'2C=O, then H3O+ --> tertiary alcohol
reactions.conditions: A Grignard reagent with a ketone.
reactions.notes: Two new carbon-carbon bonds to one carbon.

reactions.name: Grignard with an ester
reactions.equation: 2 RMgX + R'COOR'', then H3O+ --> tertiary alcohol
reactions.conditions: Excess Grignard reagent with an ester.
reactions.observation: A tertiary alcohol forms after two additions.
reactions.notes: Stopping at the ketone stage is difficult.

reactions.name: Grignard with carbon dioxide
reactions.conditions: A Grignard reagent bubbled with dry carbon dioxide.
reactions.observation: A carboxylic acid with one extra carbon forms.
reactions.notes: A route to acids from alkyl and aryl halides.

reactions.name: Sandmeyer reaction
reactions.conditions: A diazonium salt with a copper(I) halide.
reactions.observation: A nitrogen is replaced by a halogen.
reactions.notes: Converts aromatic amines into aryl halides.

reactions.name: Azo coupling
reactions.conditions: A diazonium salt with a phenol or aromatic amine.
reactions.observation: An intensely coloured azo dye forms.
reactions.notes: The basis of many azo dyes and indicators.

reactions.name: Hofmann rearrangement
reactions.conditions: A primary amide with bromine and strong base.
reactions.observation: An amine with one fewer carbon forms.
reactions.notes: Proceeds through an isocyanate intermediate.

reactions.name: Beckmann rearrangement
reactions.conditions: An oxime treated with acid.
reactions.notes: The group anti to the leaving OH migrates; the basis of nylon 6.

reactions.name: Curtius rearrangement
reactions.conditions: An acyl azide heated, then hydrolysed.
reactions.observation: An amine forms via an isocyanate.
reactions.notes: Used to make amines and protected amine intermediates.

reactions.name: Schmidt reaction
reactions.conditions: Hydrazoic acid with a carboxylic acid and acid.
reactions.observation: An amine forms with loss of carbon dioxide.
reactions.notes: Also converts ketones into amides.

reactions.name: Lossen rearrangement
reactions.conditions: An O-acyl hydroxamic acid heated, often with base.
reactions.observation: An isocyanate and then an amine form.
reactions.notes: A rearrangement related to Hofmann and Curtius.

reactions.name: Barton reaction
reactions.conditions: Irradiation of an alcohol nitrite ester.
reactions.observation: A remote C-H bond is functionalized.
reactions.notes: The basis of radical C-H activation.

reactions.name: Barton-McCombie deoxygenation
reactions.conditions: Conversion to a xanthate then radical reduction with tributyltin hydride.
reactions.observation: The hydroxyl group is replaced by hydrogen.
reactions.notes: A mild radical method to remove oxygen.

reactions.name: Hofmann-Loffler-Freytag reaction
reactions.conditions: Irradiation of an N-haloamine under acid.
reactions.observation: A remote C-H bond is halogenated.
reactions.notes: An early example of intramolecular radical C-H functionalization.

reactions.name: Wohl degradation
reactions.equation: aldose --NH2OH, then (CH3CO)2O--> aldose with one less carbon
reactions.conditions: Oxime formation then acetylation and dehydration.
reactions.observation: The carbon chain shortens by one.
reactions.notes: Used in carbohydrate structure determination.

reactions.name: Kiliani-Fischer synthesis
reactions.equation: aldose + HCN, then hydrolysis/reduction --> two epimeric aldoses
reactions.conditions: Cyanohydrin formation then reduction.
reactions.observation: The chain lengthens by one carbon, giving two epimers.
reactions.notes: Used to extend sugars; complements Wohl degradation.

reactions.name: Ruff-Fenton degradation
reactions.equation: aldose --Fe3+/H2O2--> aldose with one less carbon
reactions.conditions: Oxidation with iron(III) and hydrogen peroxide.
reactions.observation: The sugar shortens by one carbon.
reactions.notes: An alternative to the Wohl degradation.

reactions.name: Baylis-Hillman reaction
reactions.conditions: An electron-poor alkene with an aldehyde and DABCO catalyst.
reactions.notes: An atom-economical C-C bond-forming reaction.

reactions.name: Suzuki coupling
reactions.conditions: An aryl boronic acid and an aryl halide with a palladium catalyst and base.
reactions.notes: Tolerant of many functional groups; widely used in industry.

reactions.name: Heck reaction
reactions.conditions: An aryl halide and an alkene with palladium and base.
reactions.observation: An arylated alkene forms, usually the trans isomer.
reactions.notes: Awarded the 2010 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

reactions.name: Sonogashira coupling
reactions.conditions: An aryl halide and a terminal alkyne with palladium and copper.
reactions.notes: Used to build conjugated and molecular-wire compounds.

reactions.name: Stille coupling
reactions.conditions: An organotin reagent and an organic halide with palladium.
reactions.notes: Very tolerant of functional groups but the tin reagents are toxic.

reactions.name: Negishi coupling
reactions.conditions: An organozinc reagent and an organic halide with palladium or nickel.
reactions.notes: The organozinc reagent is mild and functional-group tolerant.

reactions.name: Kumada coupling
reactions.conditions: A Grignard reagent and an organic halide with nickel or palladium.
reactions.notes: An early cross-coupling using cheap magnesium reagents.

reactions.name: Buchwald-Hartwig amination
reactions.conditions: An aryl halide and an amine with palladium and a bulky phosphine ligand.
reactions.notes: A practical way to build C-N bonds.

reactions.name: Ullmann reaction
reactions.conditions: An aryl halide with copper at high temperature.
reactions.notes: Historically important for making biaryls and diarylamines.

reactions.name: Ring-closing metathesis
reactions.conditions: A diene with a ruthenium or molybdenum carbene catalyst.
reactions.observation: A ring closes with loss of ethylene.
reactions.notes: Used to build medium and large rings.

reactions.name: Cross metathesis
reactions.conditions: Two alkenes with a ruthenium carbene catalyst.
reactions.notes: Awarded the 2005 Nobel Prize; part of olefin metathesis.

reactions.name: Fischer indole synthesis
reactions.conditions: A phenylhydrazone heated with acid.
reactions.notes: A classic route to the indole alkaloid skeleton.

reactions.name: Skraup synthesis
reactions.conditions: Aniline with glycerol, sulfuric acid, and an oxidizing agent.
reactions.notes: A classical route to quinolines.

reactions.name: Paal-Knorr synthesis
reactions.conditions: A 1,4-dicarbonyl with ammonia or a primary amine.
reactions.observation: A pyrrole (or furan, or thiophene) ring forms.
reactions.notes: One of the most direct routes to these heterocycles.

reactions.name: Hantzsch pyridine synthesis
reactions.conditions: Two beta-keto esters, an aldehyde, and ammonia.
reactions.observation: A dihydropyridine forms, oxidizable to a pyridine.
reactions.notes: The route to nifedipine-type calcium channel blockers.

reactions.name: Biginelli reaction
reactions.conditions: An acid-catalysed three-component condensation.
reactions.observation: A dihydropyrimidinone forms in one pot.
reactions.notes: A multicomponent reaction valued in medicinal chemistry.

reactions.name: Bischler-Napieralski reaction
reactions.conditions: An amide cyclized with phosphorus oxychloride.
reactions.notes: Used to build isoquinoline alkaloids.

reactions.name: Pomeranz-Fritsch reaction
reactions.conditions: An acid-catalysed cyclization of an aminoacetal.
reactions.notes: A route to isoquinoline alkaloids.

reactions.name: Doebner-Miller reaction
reactions.conditions: An aniline condensed with crotonaldehyde under acid.
reactions.notes: A variant of the Skraup synthesis.

reactions.name: Chichibabin reaction
reactions.conditions: Sodium amide with pyridine at high temperature.
reactions.notes: A nucleophilic aromatic substitution on an electron-poor ring.

reactions.name: Ziegler-Natta polymerization
reactions.conditions: A titanium catalyst with an organoaluminium co-catalyst.
reactions.observation: A highly linear, stereoregular polymer forms.
reactions.notes: Made polypropylene and high-density polyethylene possible.

reactions.name: Free-radical polymerization
reactions.conditions: An initiator such as a peroxide, AIBN, or light.
reactions.observation: A high-molecular-weight polymer forms through chain growth.
reactions.notes: The most widely used industrial polymerization method.

reactions.name: Cationic polymerization
reactions.conditions: A strong acid such as BF3 with a trace of water.
reactions.notes: Used for butyl rubber and poly(vinyl ethers).

reactions.name: Ring-opening polymerization
reactions.conditions: A cyclic monomer opened by an initiator or heat.
reactions.notes: Used for nylon 6, polylactide, and polyethers.

reactions.name: Ring-opening metathesis polymerization
reactions.conditions: A cyclic olefin with a ruthenium carbene catalyst.
reactions.notes: ROMP is used for specialty elastomers.

reactions.name: Emulsion polymerization
reactions.equation: n CH2=CHCl --persulfate, surfactant, H2O--> PVC latex
reactions.conditions: Monomer dispersed in water with a surfactant and initiator.
reactions.observation: A latex of polymer particles forms.
reactions.notes: Used for PVC, paints, and adhesives.

reactions.name: Copolymerization
reactions.equation: n CH2=CH2 + n CH2=CHCH3 --> alternating/random copolymer
reactions.conditions: Two or more different monomers polymerized together.
reactions.observation: A copolymer with combined properties forms.
reactions.notes: Used for SBR rubber, ABS plastic, and many others.

reactions.name: Vulcanization
reactions.conditions: Sulfur and heat, often with accelerators.
reactions.observation: Rubber becomes harder and more elastic.
reactions.notes: Discovered by Goodyear; sulfur cross-links the chains.

reactions.name: Nylon-6,6 synthesis
reactions.conditions: Hexamethylenediamine with adipoyl chloride at an interface.
reactions.observation: A tough polymer film forms at the interface.
reactions.notes: A classic interfacial polycondensation demonstration.

reactions.name: Polyurethane synthesis
reactions.conditions: A diisocyanate reacts with a polyol.
reactions.notes: Used for foams, coatings, and adhesives.

reactions.name: PET synthesis
reactions.equation: ethylene glycol + terephthalic acid --heat--> PET + H2O
reactions.conditions: A diol and a diacid with heat and a catalyst.
reactions.notes: The basis of drinks bottles and polyester fibre.

reactions.name: Bakelite formation
reactions.conditions: Phenol and formaldehyde condensed under heat and pressure.
reactions.notes: The first fully synthetic plastic.

reactions.name: Silicone synthesis
reactions.conditions: Hydrolysis of diorganodichlorosilanes then condensation.
reactions.notes: Used for sealants, oils, and implants.

reactions.name: Aspirin synthesis
reactions.conditions: Salicylic acid acetylated with acetic anhydride.
reactions.notes: A standard undergraduate acetylation experiment.

reactions.name: Paracetamol synthesis
reactions.conditions: 4-Aminophenol acetylated with acetic anhydride.
reactions.notes: Demonstrates amide and phenol acetylation selectivity.

reactions.name: Ibuprofen synthesis
reactions.conditions: A green three-step catalytic route from isobutylbenzene.
reactions.observation: Racemic ibuprofen forms in high atom economy.
reactions.notes: Awarded the Presidential Green Chemistry Challenge.

reactions.name: Flame test
reactions.conditions: A clean wire dipped in a salt and held in a flame.
reactions.observation: Sodium is golden yellow, potassium lilac, calcium brick red, copper green.
reactions.notes: Used to identify metal cations.

reactions.name: Borax bead test
reactions.equation: borax --heat--> NaBO2 + B2O3; oxide + B2O3 --> coloured bead
reactions.conditions: A borax bead fused with a metal salt in a flame.
reactions.notes: Identifies coloured metal ions.

reactions.name: Brown ring test
reactions.conditions: Nitrate solution layered over iron(II) sulfate with sulfuric acid.
reactions.observation: A brown ring of the nitroso complex forms at the interface.
reactions.notes: Confirms the nitrate ion.

reactions.name: Chromyl chloride test
reactions.conditions: A chloride heated with dichromate and concentrated sulfuric acid.
reactions.notes: Confirms chloride in inorganic salts.

reactions.name: Nessler's test
reactions.conditions: Ammonia or ammonium salt treated with Nessler's reagent.
reactions.observation: A brown colour or precipitate shows ammonia.
reactions.notes: A sensitive test for ammonium ions.

reactions.name: Lassaigne's test
reactions.equation: organic + Na, heat --> NaCN, Na2S, NaX (fused extract)
reactions.conditions: An organic compound fused with sodium metal, then extracted with water.
reactions.observation: The extract gives tests for N, S, and halogens.
reactions.notes: A preliminary test for elements in organic compounds.

reactions.name: Charcoal cavity test
reactions.equation: metal salt + Na2CO3 --blowpipe, charcoal--> metal bead
reactions.conditions: A salt with sodium carbonate blown onto charcoal.
reactions.observation: A metal bead or coloured residue forms.
reactions.notes: A classical dry test for metal cations.

reactions.name: Cobalt nitrate test
reactions.conditions: A zinc salt with cobalt nitrate on charcoal.
reactions.observation: A green residue of cobalt zincate forms.
reactions.notes: Confirms zinc.

reactions.name: Baeyer's test
reactions.equation: alkene + cold dil. KMnO4 --> colourless + MnO2
reactions.conditions: An alkene treated with cold, dilute alkaline permanganate.
reactions.notes: Confirms unsaturation (a positive test decolourises the reagent).

reactions.name: Iodoform (haloform) test
reactions.conditions: A methyl ketone or ethanol heated with iodine and alkali.
reactions.observation: Yellow crystals of iodoform with a characteristic smell form.
reactions.notes: Detects a CH3CO group or a CH3CH(OH) group.

reactions.name: Lucas test
reactions.conditions: An alcohol with Lucas reagent (zinc chloride in concentrated HCl).
reactions.observation: Tertiary alcohols turn cloudy at once, secondary slowly, primary not at room temperature.
reactions.notes: Distinguishes primary, secondary, and tertiary alcohols.

reactions.name: 2,4-DNP test
reactions.conditions: A carbonyl compound with Brady's reagent.
reactions.notes: Confirms an aldehyde or ketone and gives a sharp melting point.

reactions.name: Fehling's test
reactions.conditions: An aldehyde heated with Fehling's solution.
reactions.observation: A red precipitate of copper(I) oxide forms.
reactions.notes: Ketones give no reaction; used to tell aldehydes from ketones.

reactions.name: Benedict's test
reactions.conditions: A reducing sugar heated with Benedict's solution.
reactions.observation: A red, orange, or green precipitate forms.
reactions.notes: Detects reducing sugars in urine and food.

reactions.name: Molisch's test
reactions.conditions: A carbohydrate with alpha-naphthol and concentrated sulfuric acid.
reactions.observation: A violet ring forms at the interface.
reactions.notes: A general test for carbohydrates.

reactions.name: Biuret test
reactions.equation: peptide + Cu2+ in alkali --> violet complex
reactions.conditions: A protein with copper(II) sulfate and sodium hydroxide.
reactions.observation: A violet colour shows peptide bonds.
reactions.notes: A general test for proteins.

reactions.name: Xanthoproteic test
reactions.equation: aromatic protein + conc. HNO3 --> yellow nitro-protein
reactions.conditions: A protein with concentrated nitric acid, then ammonia.
reactions.observation: A yellow colour deepens to orange with ammonia.
reactions.notes: Detects aromatic amino-acid residues.

reactions.name: Millon's test
reactions.conditions: A protein with Millon's reagent (mercury in nitric acid).
reactions.observation: A white precipitate turns red on heating.
reactions.notes: Detects the phenolic group of tyrosine.

reactions.name: Ninhydrin test
reactions.conditions: An amino acid or protein spotted with ninhydrin and heated.
reactions.observation: A blue-violet colour forms (yellow with proline).
reactions.notes: Used to visualise amino acids on chromatography paper.

reactions.name: Seliwanoff's test
reactions.conditions: A sugar heated with Seliwanoff's reagent.
reactions.observation: Ketohexoses give a cherry-red colour faster than aldoses.
reactions.notes: Distinguishes ketoses from aldoses.

reactions.name: Osazone formation
reactions.conditions: A reducing sugar with phenylhydrazine heated in acid.
reactions.observation: Characteristic yellow crystals with sharp melting points form.
reactions.notes: Used to identify sugars.

reactions.name: Kjeldahl digestion
reactions.conditions: A sample digested with sulfuric acid and a catalyst.
reactions.observation: Nitrogen is converted into ammonium sulfate.
reactions.notes: The basis of protein nitrogen determination.

reactions.name: Dumas method
reactions.equation: nitrogenous sample + CuO, heat --> N2 gas measured
reactions.conditions: A sample burned with copper(II) oxide and the nitrogen gas collected.
reactions.observation: The volume of nitrogen gives the nitrogen content.
reactions.notes: An alternative to the Kjeldahl method.

reactions.name: Combustion analysis
reactions.conditions: A sample burned in excess oxygen and the gases absorbed and weighed.
reactions.observation: Masses of CO2 and H2O give the empirical formula.
reactions.notes: The classical Liebig method for organic formula determination.

reactions.name: Silver nitrate halide test
reactions.conditions: Silver nitrate added to a halide solution.
reactions.observation: AgCl is white, AgBr cream, and AgI yellow.
reactions.notes: Distinguishes chloride, bromide, and iodide.

reactions.name: Barium chloride sulfate test
reactions.conditions: Barium chloride added to a solution acidified with HCl.
reactions.observation: A white precipitate insoluble in acid forms.
reactions.notes: Confirms the sulfate ion.

reactions.name: Limewater test for carbon dioxide
reactions.conditions: A gas bubbled through limewater.
reactions.notes: Confirms carbon dioxide; the cloudiness clears with excess CO2.

reactions.name: Iodometric titration
reactions.conditions: Iodine titrated with standard sodium thiosulfate, starch indicator.
reactions.observation: The blue starch colour disappears at the endpoint.
reactions.notes: Used to measure oxidising agents indirectly.

reactions.name: Permanganate titration
reactions.conditions: Potassium permanganate added to an acidified reductant.
reactions.observation: The purple colour persists at the endpoint (self-indicating).
reactions.notes: A standard redox titration.

reactions.name: Dichromate titration
reactions.conditions: Potassium dichromate with a redox indicator such as diphenylamine.
reactions.observation: A colour change marks the endpoint.
reactions.notes: Dichromate is a primary standard.

reactions.name: Complexometric titration
reactions.conditions: A metal solution titrated with EDTA and a metal indicator such as Eriochrome Black T.
reactions.observation: The indicator changes colour at the endpoint.
reactions.notes: Used to determine water hardness and metal ions.

reactions.name: Acid-base titration
reactions.conditions: An acid titrated with a base (or vice versa) to an indicator endpoint.
reactions.observation: The indicator changes colour at the equivalence point.
reactions.notes: The basis of volumetric analysis.

reactions.name: Haber-Bosch process
reactions.conditions: Iron catalyst with promoters at high pressure and moderate temperature.
reactions.observation: Ammonia forms in a yield limited by equilibrium.
reactions.notes: Feeds the world's fertiliser supply.

reactions.name: Ostwald process
reactions.conditions: Ammonia oxidised over a platinum-rhodium gauze at about 800 degrees.
reactions.observation: Nitric oxide forms, then nitric acid.
reactions.notes: The industrial route to nitric acid.

reactions.name: Contact process
reactions.conditions: Sulfur dioxide oxidised over vanadium(V) oxide at about 450 degrees.
reactions.observation: Sulfur trioxide forms, absorbed to give sulfuric acid.
reactions.notes: The main industrial route to sulfuric acid.

reactions.name: Birkeland-Eyde process
reactions.conditions: Air passed through an electric arc above 3000 degrees.
reactions.observation: Nitric oxide forms from nitrogen and oxygen.
reactions.notes: An early, energy-intensive nitrogen fixation method.

reactions.name: Fischer-Tropsch process
reactions.equation: n CO + 2n H2 --Fe or Co--> (-CH2-)n + n H2O
reactions.conditions: Syngas over an iron or cobalt catalyst at moderate temperature and pressure.
reactions.notes: Converts coal or gas into liquid fuels.

reactions.name: Bergius process
reactions.equation: coal + H2 --Fe, high T, high P--> liquid hydrocarbons
reactions.conditions: Coal hydrogenated at high temperature and pressure.
reactions.notes: An early coal liquefaction method.

reactions.name: Kraft process
reactions.equation: wood + NaOH/Na2S, heat --> cellulose pulp + lignin
reactions.conditions: Wood chips cooked in alkaline sodium hydroxide and sulfide liquor.
reactions.notes: The dominant chemical pulping method.

reactions.name: Claus process
reactions.conditions: Hydrogen sulfide partly burned to sulfur dioxide, then reacted over a catalyst.
reactions.notes: Recovers sulfur from oil and gas refining.

reactions.name: Solvay process
reactions.equation: NaCl + NH3 + CO2 + H2O --> NaHCO3 + NH4Cl
reactions.conditions: Ammonia and carbon dioxide passed into brine.
reactions.observation: Sodium bicarbonate precipitates; heating gives sodium carbonate.
reactions.notes: The major route to soda ash.

reactions.name: Chlor-alkali process
reactions.conditions: Electrolysis of brine in a membrane cell.
reactions.observation: Chlorine, hydrogen, and sodium hydroxide form together.
reactions.notes: One of the largest electrochemical industries.

reactions.name: Hall-Heroult process
reactions.conditions: Alumina dissolved in molten cryolite, electrolysed with carbon anodes.
reactions.observation: Molten aluminium collects at the cathode.
reactions.notes: The only large-scale route to aluminium metal.

reactions.name: Bessemer process
reactions.conditions: Air blown through molten pig iron in a converter.
reactions.observation: Carbon and impurities burn off, leaving steel.
reactions.notes: The first cheap mass production of steel.

reactions.name: Blast furnace ironmaking
reactions.conditions: Iron ore, coke, and limestone heated with hot air.
reactions.observation: Molten iron and slag are tapped separately.
reactions.notes: The main route from ore to pig iron.

reactions.name: Steam reforming
reactions.conditions: Methane and steam over a nickel catalyst.
reactions.notes: The main industrial source of hydrogen.

reactions.name: Catalytic cracking
reactions.equation: long-chain alkane --zeolite, heat--> shorter alkenes + alkanes
reactions.conditions: Heavy petroleum fractions over a zeolite catalyst.
reactions.observation: Smaller, more valuable hydrocarbons and alkenes form.
reactions.notes: Supplies petrol and petrochemical feedstocks.

reactions.name: Catalytic reforming
reactions.equation: alkane --Pt, heat--> branched alkane + aromatics + H2
reactions.conditions: Naphtha over a platinum catalyst with hydrogen.
reactions.observation: Higher-octane branched and aromatic hydrocarbons form.
reactions.notes: Improves petrol quality.

reactions.name: Water-gas shift reaction
reactions.conditions: Carbon monoxide and steam over an iron or copper catalyst.
reactions.notes: Adjusts the H2/CO ratio of syngas.

reactions.name: Fermentation of glucose
reactions.conditions: Glucose with yeast enzymes, anaerobically.
reactions.notes: The basis of brewing and baking.

reactions.name: Glycolysis
reactions.equation: glucose + 2 NAD+ + 2 ADP --> 2 pyruvate + 2 NADH + 2 ATP
reactions.conditions: Enzymes in the cytoplasm, without oxygen.
reactions.observation: Glucose is split and a little ATP is made.
reactions.notes: The first stage of cellular respiration.

reactions.name: Light reactions of photosynthesis
reactions.equation: 2 H2O + 2 NADP+ + light --> O2 + 2 NADPH + 2 H+
reactions.conditions: Chlorophyll in the thylakoid membrane absorbs light.
reactions.observation: Water is split, oxygen is released, and NADPH and ATP form.
reactions.notes: Provides energy for carbon fixation.

reactions.name: Calvin cycle
reactions.conditions: Enzymes in the chloroplast stroma, using ATP and NADPH.
reactions.observation: Carbon dioxide is fixed into a three-carbon sugar.
reactions.notes: The light-independent stage of photosynthesis.

reactions.name: Citric acid (Krebs) cycle
reactions.equation: acetyl-CoA + 3 NAD+ + FAD + GDP --> 2 CO2 + 3 NADH + FADH2 + GTP
reactions.conditions: Enzymes in the mitochondrial matrix.
reactions.observation: Acetyl groups are fully oxidised to carbon dioxide.
reactions.notes: The central hub of aerobic metabolism.

reactions.name: Urea cycle
reactions.conditions: Enzymes in the liver mitochondria and cytosol.
reactions.observation: Toxic ammonia is converted into urea for excretion.
reactions.notes: Removes nitrogen waste in mammals.

reactions.name: Beta-oxidation
reactions.equation: fatty acyl-CoA + FAD + NAD+ + CoA --> acetyl-CoA + FADH2 + NADH
reactions.conditions: Enzymes in the mitochondrial matrix.
reactions.observation: Fatty acids are shortened two carbons at a time.
reactions.notes: Releases energy from fats.

reactions.name: Anaerobic digestion
reactions.conditions: Microbes break down waste without oxygen.
reactions.notes: Used to treat waste and produce renewable gas.
